candidate_windows.window_text: We benchmark the performance of diverse baselines on MT-RAIG BENCH. For multi-table retrieval, we consider both general-purpose retriever (Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009; Karpukhin et al., 2020; Izacard et al., 2021), and table-specific retriever (Herzig et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023) as the baselines. For insight generation, we employ 11 LLM-based baselines including proprietary (OpenAI, 2025b, 2024; Anthropic), open-source (DeepSeek-AI, 2025; Yang et al., 2024; Mesnard et al., 2024; MetaAI, 2024; Jiang et al., 2023), and SOTA-TQA methods (Ye et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024b; Zhao et al., 2024) for comprehensive evaluations. The results are shown in Table 4 and Table 6, respectively. Please refer to Appendix B for the detailed information on the experimental setup and all the baselines.

Table Input Localization Following recent studies that utilize language models for table-related tasks (Chen, 2023; Seo et al., 2024), we serialize the table input into a flattened sequence to effectively represent table data for language model processing. The table title is enclosed within [TITLE] tags, followed by the table headers marked with [HEADER], where individual column names are separated by a vertical bar ( | ). Each row

is prefixed with a [ROW] tag and an index, while cell values are separated by a vertical bar. This approach ensures that the table format is preserved while making the input compatible with language models. For example, the input table is formatted as follows:

[TITLE] title [HEADER] col1 | col2 | ... [ROW 1] cell1,1 | cell1,2 | ... [ROW 2] cell2,1 | ...

Training and Inference For the table-specific retriever, we fine-tune each model on a single-table QA dataset using the AdamW optimizer with a learning rate of for 5 epochs. To efficiently fine-tune the model, we adopt LoRA and set the parameters as $r = 8$ , $\alpha = 32$ . We use a constant learning rate schedule set at 2e-5, and train with the batch size of 1 on 4 NVIDIA A100 GPU. The inference of open-source LLMs are conducted using vLLM framework (Kwon et al., 2023). We set temperature to 0.0 for efficient and robust output generation.

To supplement Table 5, we present the Spearman correlation results alongside the Pearson correlation, in terms of faithfulness and completeness, as shown in Table 17. We report the full multitable retrieval results in Table 19, MT-RAIG EVAL Completeness score results of diverse baselines in Table 20, with respect to Precision, Recall, and F1 score across different top- $k$ values. Additionally, we present insight generation results along with existing automatic metrics in Table 21.
